worthwhile_why: The decisive move was resolving a size-guard test failure: bumping daemon_config.py's line budget with a dated ledger entry and keeping the docstring tight. Executing that legitimately rests on a stored cross-session convention (size guards are 'bump-with-approval' stale thresholds, bump for small additions / split only when chronic, rationale at the decision site) — not purely the in-moment options menu.
needed_knowledge: Size-guardrail line-limit tests in this repo are deliberate but stale thresholds with a documented 'bump-with-your-approval' history — bumping one (with a dated reason) after operator approval is the established, blessed pattern, not a way to dodge a quality gate.

The bump-vs-split heuristic: for a small addition (here ~23 lines, the worktree helper) raising the limit is the right call; splitting the file is only warranted when a file is chronically hitting its limit. This is exactly the fork the move had to decide.

Code-style preference on where rationale lives: justify by caller/purpose and keep the 'why' at the decision site rather than padding a docstring — which is the reversal the outcome took (docstring kept tight, churn rationale moved to daemon_client._code_changed).
Test-integrity rule: don't modify a guard test until the operator approves (already satisfied in-session by 'yes :)').
